turns.content: Calculate the initial moles in 20.00 cm3 of 0.050 M acetic acid and the volume of 0.100 M NaOH required for equivalence after adding 20.00 cm3 of water.
At one-quarter of the equivalence volume, calculate the remaining acid-derived species and neutralization product using the acid and reaction established above.
Use Ka=1.85e-5 and the buffer composition calculated at one-quarter equivalence to determine the pH.
At the equivalence point implied by the preceding stoichiometry, calculate the total solution volume and concentration of the product species.
Write the hydrolysis equilibrium for the product species present at equivalence and derive the required relation among its equilibrium constants.
Using Kw=1.00e-14 where needed for that equilibrium, calculate the controlling species concentration and the equivalence-point pH.
Report the one-quarter-equivalence pH followed by the equivalence-point pH.
Check that dilution was handled consistently and verify the equivalence result against the equilibrium model and assumptions used in the preceding steps.
Report the one-quarter-equivalence and equivalence-point pH values in that order, identifying the buffer and hydrolysis regimes used.
